title: APIServer: avoid recreating etcd clients on every metrics scrape
human_review:
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] Nit: if shutdownCh were ever nil (receiving on a nil channel blocks forever), this
goroutine would leak and keep cache alive indefinitely.
ShutdownInitiatedNotify() currently always returns a non-nil channel via Signaled(), but a defensive nil check would make this more robust against future changes.

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] `ShutdownInitiatedNotify()` is signaled at **T0** in the shutdown sequence — immediately
when the KILL signal is received. At this point, in-flight requests (including Prometheus
metric scrapes) are still being served and drained.

The shutdown sequence is:

| Phase | Event | What happens |
|-------|-------|-------------|
| T0 | `ShutdownInitiated` | KILL signal received, `/readyz` goes red |
| T1 | `AfterShutdownDelayDuration` | Delay period elapsed |
| T2 | `NotAcceptingNewRequest` | Server stops accepting new connections |
| T3 | `InFlightRequestsDrained` | All in-flight HTTP handlers have returned |

By closing the monitor cache at **T0**, any metrics scrape that happens between **T0** and
**T3** will receive a `"monitor cache is closed"` error instead of actual storage size
metrics. This is a **regression in behavior** — the old code (create-use-close per scrape)
would have continued to work fine during the entire drain period.

I think this should use `c.DrainedNotify()` instead, which signals at **T3** after all
in-flight requests have completed. That way the cached monitors remain available for the
full duration of graceful shutdown:

```go
metrics.SetStorageMonitorGetter(monitorGetter(factory, c.DrainedNotify()))
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] Move all this code into cache struct and split into methods
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] Done, split into separate methods.
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] Thanks for pointing this out — updated to use `c.DrainedNotify()`.
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] Thanks — added a nil check and unit tests as well.

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] splitting responsibility for constructing and cleaning up the clients between a closure and a cache instance is hard to follow

I'd suggest putting all the responsibility in the cache instance, requiring the drained / stop channel (returning an error from `newMonitorCache` if stopCh is nil), and constructing like this:

```go
monitorCache, err := newMonitorCache(factory, c.DrainedNotify())
if err != nil {
  return nil, err
}
metrics.SetStorageMonitorGetter(monitorCache.get)
```

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] naming with a `Locked` suffix typically means it must only be called under lock. Since this take a lock internally, drop the `Locked` suffix from the name
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] Thanks, makes sense. I’ve moved the lifecycle ownership into `monitorCache`.
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] move the goroutine setup into `initialize()` after assigning to `c.monitors = monitors` so we don't spin up goroutines we never need
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/etcd.go] Thanks @liggitt. Fixed.

Thanks for working on this.

One concern: `ShutdownInitiatedNotify()` fires at **T0** — immediately on KILL signal. But in-flight requests (including Prometheus scrapes) continue for up to **130 seconds** after that before [`InFlightRequestsDrained`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/lifecycle_signals.go#L57-L62) is signaled. Any scrape in that window will get `"monitor cache is closed"` instead of metrics. Could you use `c.DrainedNotify()` instead?

Also, could you add **unit tests** for the `monitorCache`? Specifically: caching across calls,
post-close error, concurrent first-init, and retry after transient failure.

human_review: [test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] I can see arguments both ways on this one.  I've framed the wording around the most common behavior.

[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] I think this is a foot gun and I'd want future types to default to not allowing it ... SSA would be my recommendation for applying an update without knowing the current resource version
[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] I think these would fall under "grandfathered with no clear rationale" as well

[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] events are best effort (auto-deleted after O(hours)), multi-write, and high-write-volume, so making them cheaper to create was useful
[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] endpoints were frequently written and high volume, so supporting upsert was specifically desired

[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] This allowlist doesn't look correct to me.

Storage implementations can:
* not implement DefaultGarbageCollectionPolicy (which makes requests do background deletion by default, which we want)
* implement DefaultGarbageCollectionPolicy and return OrphanDependents (which makes requests do orphaning deletion by default, which we don't want)
* implement DefaultGarbageCollectionPolicy and return DeleteDependents (which makes requests do foreground deletion by default, which we don't want)
* implement DefaultGarbageCollectionPolicy and return Unsupported (which prevents the deleter from requesting orphan or foreground deletion, which we maybe don't want)

I only see eight storage implementations of DefaultGarbageCollectionPolicy, so this allowlist should only have eight types in it (+group variants):
* daemonset
* deployment
* replicaset
* statefulset
* cronjob
* job
* event
* replicationcontroller

We also don't generally *want* new types to implement DefaultGarbageCollectionPolicy to force foreground deletion by default.
[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] where are you seeing OrphanDependents default for these types?
[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] where are you seeing OrphanDependents default for these types?

I configured the test to only test served APIs, so some of the APIs in the above list get skipped for this reason, but I've verified that all versions are now correctly tested, so if we need to do per-version exemptions in the future, we can.

There was a gap in the test for events, since it uses the "Unsupported" garbage collection strategy. I've added test coverage for that.
[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/fields_wiping_test.go] do you want to squash the standardization commit down into https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138163 ?
[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] maybe document that and move endpoints and events out of the "no clear rationale" section?
[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] move RBAC into the "no clear rationale" section and drop this comment

[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] new resources that require the name to be derived from particular field values would be a legitimate reason to extend this list, but not for any other reason

[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] the polarity on this (and the allowlist) seems backwards to me ... I think new resources should set AllowUnconditionalUpdate() == false and require SSA to update without specifying RV
[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] do we also want to detect resources that default to foreground deletion and discourage that in the future?
[test/integration/apiserver/apidefinitions/default_behaviors_test.go] I'm confused why this is in the unsupported list ... namespace doesn't implement DefaultGarbageCollectionPolicy that I can see

Thanks for this addition @dalefrieswthat! The approach of testing NodePort connectivity under a deny-all-ingress NetworkPolicy is solid. A few suggestions to strengthen the test:

### 1. Add a wait for Service endpoint readiness (Medium)
After creating the NodePort service, the test immediately probes connectivity. There's a race window where kube-proxy/iptables rules haven't been installed yet — meaning the test could pass because the NodePort path isn't functional yet, not because NetworkPolicy blocked it.

**Suggestion**: Add an endpoint readiness poll (e.g., `framework.WaitForServiceEndpointsNum`) before testing connectivity, or at minimum document why the race is acceptable.

### 2. Only validates from in-cluster pods (Medium)
The test title references "north/south" traffic, but validation uses `agnhost connect` from pods inside the cluster. With `externalTrafficPolicy=Local`, in-cluster NodePort behavior may differ from genuine external traffic due to hairpin/SNAT differences.

**Suggestion**: Clarify in the test name/comment that this tests "NodePort path from in-cluster clients" to set accurate expectations.

### 3. Only tests the node where the pod runs (Medium)
Because `externalTrafficPolicy=Local`, hitting the NodePort on a node *without* the target pod would drop the packet (no local endpoint). The test only targets `targetPod.Status.HostIP` — the node where the pod IS running. This means we can't distinguish "blocked by NetworkPolicy" from "dropped by externalTrafficPolicy."

**Suggestion**: Add a secondary probe against a *different* node's IP to disambiguate NetworkPolicy blocking from externalTrafficPolicy dropping.

### 4. Add `defer` cleanup for the Service (Low)
The created service `nodeport-isolated-pod` is never explicitly deleted. Namespace teardown handles it, but a `defer` delete would be more consistent with other test patterns.

### 5. Consider LoadBalancer coverage (Gap)
The original issue mentions both NodePort and LoadBalancer. This PR only covers NodePort — a follow-up PR for LoadBalancer testing would complete the coverage.

Overall this is a good contribution. Issues 1 and 3 are the most important since they affect test correctness. Looking forward to the next iteration!

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/metrics/TROUBLESHOOTING.md] The pipeline diagram lists `cacheWatcher.result` as the final stage, but the instrumentation currently ends at `cacheWatcher.input`. The `sendWatchCacheEvent` path between input and result includes `convertToWatchEvent` (object serialization/conversion) and the write to the `c.result` channel.

would it be worthwhile adding a metric for this final stage so that operators can distinguish between slow object conversion and a blocked client connection when step 5 exhibits high values?

title: test/e2e: relax PLR convergence checks after resize
human_review:
[test/e2e/common/node/framework/podresize/resize.go] Checking for 0 won't account for the cases that were deflaked in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/131055.

To account for cases that the restart happens (unrelated to the resize) before the resize patch is issues, we call UpdateExpectedContainerRestarts before the resize patch:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0d28578de14fce641a39d6415d2068e1f39283a4/test/e2e/common/node/framework/podresize/resize.go#L474-L479

All that to say, I think instead of checking `if wantRestartCount == 0`, we might want to check `if (!restartExpected && wantRestartCount != gotRestartCount)`

[test/e2e/common/node/framework/podresize/resize.go] I'm trying to think about this. Does this flake only happen in PLR-related resize tests? We don't expect it to restart more than once in restart cases, so if this is happening frequently only for PLR resizes (and not container-only resizes), I wonder if that indicates an actual issue that needs to be fixed?

/cc @ndixita

[test/e2e/common/node/framework/podresize/resize.go] I don't think we should ignore this. We've seen in the past failures where kubelet incorrectly never clears the resize conditions, and this is a real issue that should cause the test to fail. The lingering should be at most 2 minutes, and the timeout I believe is generous enough to allow that.

[pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/preemption.go] I'll add field "name" into domain struct

[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption.go] I'll create a separate branch that will use provided mock for workload case

[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption_test.go] Is not valid anymore for current impl. For now algorithm is going to preempt all pods less that or equal some min priority N.

```
      For the remaining potential victims, using binary search across priorities find the minimal
      priority N for which scheduling the preemptor can be achieved without preempting any victims
      with priority higher than N. This allows to reduce the potential cascaiding preemptions later.
```
[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption_test.go] We cannot select which pods for the same priority we should keep or drop
[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption_test.go] No more valid anymore, as mentioned: We cannot select which pods for the same priority we should keep or drop

[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption_test.go] Current implementation cannot guarantee ordering for NonViolating pods because of binary search for priorities. Some ordering can be applied for pdb violating pods, adopted test for that scenario
[pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/preemption.go] What preemptionPolicy should be used? Workload level or pod level aggregated in some way? What about inconsistencies for preemptionPolicy?

[pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/preemption.go] I believe it was supposed to be covered by preemptionPriority. So for workloads that are not supposed to preempt other you would set very low preemptionPriority (https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/5711#discussion_r2592606205). For now let's say that workload can always preempt other pods/workloads. (it should be good enough for alpha)

[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption.go] It should not be possible. If a pod is accessible here, it needs to be assumed in scheduler cache, so it's either in a binding phase or running. In both cases it should have the node name set.

[pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/preemption.go] Maybe instead of returning the preemption policy via method, we could have a method that works like PodEligibleToPreemptOthers? And here just call preemptor.EligibleToPreemptOthers()

[pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/preemption.go] For now, I would not use potentialNodes calculated from NodesForStatusCode for workload. My understanding is that NodeToStatusReader  is based on the list of unschedulable nodes returned from filter plugins. Not sure if this will be applicable for workloads. For now I would just return all nodes in the cluster as a Domain.

[pkg/scheduler/framework/preemption/preemption.go] I think we can keep it? We just have to make sure that klog.KObj(preemptor) will output some sensible string for both: single pod preemptor and workload preemptor.
[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption.go] Nit, move definition closer to the actual usage of the variable.

[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption.go] It seems that this binary search algorithm will work but I believe we can do even better. 

Let's say that we have 10 pods that are potential victims. We should start by adding first 5 to the domain. If everything is okay, we go right and add half of the remaining pods. If the check failed, we go left and remove half of the pods we added. This logic minimizes the number of addPods/removePods calls.

VIII. Iterate over the list of potential victims (in the order achieved with sorting above) checking if they can be placed where they are currently running. If so assume it back and remove from potential victims list.
```

[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption.go] The implementation here is intentional. Before applying binary search to find the minimum priority required for domain feasibility, we sort the candidates by priority.
On the Greedy Reprieval step we are working on remaining victims sorted by provided criteria.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136577/changes#diff-06607f15768495cdfff1d66f563e0c7ca8b761f6ec3a3b4b4e6d3c8b6c4cc2b9R437-R442

[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/defaultpreemption/default_preemption.go] We strictly cannot use a break here because PreemptionUnit is treated as an atomic unit-either all pods are preempted, or none are.

Since pdbsAllowed is a shared state tracking the remaining budget across all victims, we must iterate through every pod in the unit to correctly decrement their respective PDB counters. If we break early on the first violating pod, we fail to update the budget for the remaining pods in that unit. This corrupts the state for subsequent victims, effectively hiding potential violations for other PDBs.

This step is an optimization designed to minimize potential cascading preemptions. We consider this an expected trade-off to minimize cascading preemption chains.

human_review: [staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate/limits_test.go] I don't believe json schema allows maxProperties to be `-1`.  Testing that the limit check still works for this is fine, but a comment explaining seems justified.

[staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/validators/limits.go] I'd prefer we consistently either use golang terminology such as "map" and "element", or we consistently use JSON schema terminology such as "object" and "properties".

Or, we could explain it explicitly in both terms, e.g.:

"maxProperties provides a limit on properties of an object as defined by JSON schema.  In Kubernetes is may only be used to constrain the number of elements on a field defined as a golang map.".
[staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate/limits_test.go] For completeness, let's also test the upper bound (max int).

[staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/validators/limits.go] Updated the `Description:` to use both terms explicitly with the text suggested: 

> "maxProperties provides a limit on properties of an object as defined by JSON schema. In Kubernetes it may only be used to constrain the number of elements on a field defined as a golang map."

[staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate/limits_test.go] Yes sorry, good point I should have explained the friction I hit more and how I ended up with those test cases as you have a good point they don't test the most important edge cases w.r.t. `math.MaxInt`directly.  When I attempted to create a map with `math.MaxInt` (as well as `math.MaxInt - 1`) properties in Go, the way the test is currently constructed it creates actual maps and requires allocating that many elements.  For these cases this causes a timeout panic initializing the math.MaxInt size map (2^(63-1))

Example:
```go
              {
		name:       "math.MaxInt property, max MaxInt-1",
		properties: math.MaxInt,
		max:        math.MaxInt - 1,
		wantErrs: field.ErrorList{
			field.TooMany(field.NewPath("fldpath"), math.MaxInt, math.MaxInt-1).WithOrigin("maxProperties"),
		},
              }
```
logs: https://gist.github.com/aaron-prindle/4ec33aadfbd60354fa7cd4b0b0ed39e0
log snippet w/ the timeout:
```
panic: test timed out after 30s
	running tests:
		TestMaxProperties (30s)
		TestMaxProperties/math.MaxInt_property,_max_MaxInt-1 (30s)
```

As Go's `len()` function only works on actual built-in maps and can't be directly mocked IIUC, it is non-trivial to practically create a map w/ math.MaxInt size to trigger the failure condition for `max: math.MaxInt - 1`.

The tests cases there w/ `properties: [0|1]` + `max: math.MaxInt` were an attempt to use math.MaxInt w/ empty and set maps to hit some testing surface but understandably this doesn't hit the edge as noted. 

I believe the alternative options to make the test work here would be.  Most have a drawback or are overly complex vs keeping the valdiator itself as is.  For modifying the test only we can use `unsafe` to spoof a  large map but using unsafe :

1. Update `MaxProperties` to accept `any` and use reflection to get the length.
    - **Drawback w/ this approach**: This avoids any changes to the `validation-gen` framework (map can be passed as `any`). However there is performance penalty at runtime as it relies on reflection to determine the map's length.
2. Instead of passing the map itself to the validation function, we could update the function signature to just accept the length of the map.
    - **Drawback w/ this approach**: Need to update validation-gen framework to pass in len(obj) for this (non-trivial change but definitely do-able).
3. We could do some `unsafe` pointer hack and spoof the map length while not actually creating a large map.


Going to keep this as is for now, lmk if there is an option you prefer from this or if you had any alternative ideas here for how to test this case.  Thanks!

[staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate/limits_test.go] Actually I think it is likely ok to use the `unsafe` method and spoof the map to be large.  I see `unsafe` used in other tests in k/k so I don't think it is an anti-pattern here.  I've updated the tests cases as suggested now and have opted to use `unsafe` to spoof the large map to support the test cases.

[staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate/limits_test.go] The fact that we can't produce a test for the max says something about the max.  Should we put our own artificial limit on the highest value maxProperties can be set to?

[staging/src/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/validate/limits_test.go] SG. I doubt anyone will complain, and if they think they need more than 100,000, we should probably be having a conversation about it.

[test/cmd/exec.sh] Actually, this line isn't working as expected. I've tried this locally and when I change the kubectl invocation not to have `--`, like so: `kubectl exec -it pod-test -c container-a echo "test" 2>&1)` this then produced the expected error: 
```
error: exec [POD] [COMMAND] is not supported anymore. Use exec [POD] -- [COMMAND] instead See 'kubectl exec -h' for help and examples
```
but it wasn't properly caught by this test. That is because under the covers this function uses grep, and for grep to work correctly with special characters (like `[]`) in this case we need to escape them, with `\`. [staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create.go] I guess a downside of leaving the `cmd` parameter in place is that it makes it easy for someone to come along and re-add a dependency on cmd in the future, resulting in the same issue again.

I think what's bugging me is that `cmd` isn't a "true dependency" of create... It's only purpose is for [constructing EditOptions](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/500ceb2c5c5b782b5021a18b44f6cd1aab7b3b22/staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create.go#L296-L313)

What would it look like if we made `EditOptions` be part of `CreateOptions` build the `EditOptions` in `CreateOptions.Complete()` which already has a cmd argument?  We could even populate the default values for `EditOptions` in `NewCreateOptions()`

So adding this field to `CreateOptions`...
```go
type CreateOptions struct {
    ...
    
    EditOptions *editor.EditOptions
    
    ...
}
```

And then we can remove `cmd` from `RunCreate()`...

```go
func (o *CreateOptions) RunCreate(f cmdutil.Factory) error {
    ...

    if o.EditBeforeCreate {
        return o.EditOptions.Run() // Now we can simply invoke o.EditOptions.Run() because the options have already been populated    
    }
    
    ...
}
```

And then I also think we can get rid of `RunEditOnCreate()` at that point (or at least deprecate it in case we need to preserve it for some reason because it is exported currently).

I know that is a lot of stuff I just put out there, but I am trying to find the root cause as to why this situation is awkward and I think it is because we're trying to populate EditOptions in the wrong spot.

[staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create.go] Let's go ahead and delete this func.  Nothing else in k/k uses it, and even though it is exported, I can't think of a way that someone would call this independently of `RunCreate()`.  So it is useless now.

[staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/cmd/create/create_test.go] Done, thanks for the standard enforcement!!

+package apidefinitions
+
+import (
+	"reflect"
+)
+
+// containsAll tests is a Kubernetes unstructured value is a strict subset of another
+// unstructured value. containsAll returns true if subset equals value, or if all
+// map and slices values in subset also exist in value.
+func containsAll(subset, value any) bool {
+	if subset == nil {
+		return value == nil
+	}
+	switch subsetValue := subset.(type) {
+	case map[string]any:
+		valueMap, ok := value.(map[string]any)
+		if !ok {
+			return false
+		}
+		for k, v := range subsetValue {
+			sv, exists := valueMap[k]
+			if !exists || !containsAll(v, sv) {
+				return false
+			}
+		}
+		return true
+	case []any:
+		valueSlice, ok := value.([]any)
+		if !ok {
+			return false
+		}
+		for _, v := range subsetValue {
+			matched := false
+			for _, sv := range valueSlice {
+				if containsAll(v, sv) {
+					matched = true
+					break
+				}
+			}
+			if !matched {
+				return false
+			}
+		}
+		return true
+	default:
+		return reflect.DeepEqual(subset, value)
+	}
+}

+// blockLogger is a rate-limited logger that tracks how long a watchChan is blocked.
+type blockLogger struct {
+	interval      time.Duration
+	threshold     time.Duration
+	msg           string
+	objectType    string
+	groupResource schema.GroupResource
+
+	clock clock.Clock
+
+	mu          sync.Mutex
+	lastLogTime time.Time
+	eventCount  int
+	timeWaiting time.Duration
+}
+
+func newBlockLogger(interval time.Duration, threshold time.Duration, msg string, objectType string, groupResource schema.GroupResource, clock clock.Clock) *blockLogger {
+	l := &blockLogger{
+		interval:      interval,
+		threshold:     threshold,
+		msg:           msg,
+		objectType:    objectType,
+		groupResource: groupResource,
+		clock:         clock,
+	}
+	l.lastLogTime = l.clock.Now()
+	return l
+}
+
+func (l *blockLogger) recordWait(waitTime time.Duration) {
+	l.mu.Lock()
+	defer l.mu.Unlock()
+
+	l.eventCount++
+	l.timeWaiting += waitTime
+
+	now := l.clock.Now()
+	window := now.Sub(l.lastLogTime)
+	if window < l.interval {
+		return
+	}
+
+	if l.timeWaiting > l.threshold {
+		klog.V(3).InfoS(l.msg,
+			"objectType", l.objectType,
+			"groupResource", l.groupResource,
+			"eventCount", l.eventCount,
+			"timeWaiting", l.timeWaiting,
+			"window", window,
+		)
+	}
+	l.eventCount = 0
+	l.timeWaiting = 0
+	l.lastLogTime = now
+}

+func ParseSignedInt(val string, bitSize int) (int64, error) {
+	intVal, err := strconv.ParseInt(val, 10, 64)
+	if err != nil {
+		return 0, fmt.Errorf("parsing %q as int: %w", val, err)

+	}

+	var minVal, maxVal int64
+	switch bitSize {
+	case 8:
+		minVal, maxVal = math.MinInt8, math.MaxInt8
+	case 16:
+		minVal, maxVal = math.MinInt16, math.MaxInt16
+	case 32:

+	case 64:

+	default:
+		return 0, fmt.Errorf("unsupported bitSize %d; must be 8, 16, 32, or 64", bitSize)

title: api: enable optionalorrequired linter for resource API
human_review:
[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] There is an epic issue https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/134671 enabling Kube-API-Linter rules, which we somehow ignored for most of API groups before because of unresolved errors. Let me know if this makes sense to you. Otherwise we can start a discussion there.

Yeah I think you are right. Let me add a release note.

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] @JoelSpeed: can you point me to documentation for the `optionalorrequired` linter?

The table in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/134671 only says "All fields should be tagged either optional or required." - according to that, a `Count int` also needs either `+optional` or `+required`.
[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] @troychiu: you don't need a release note. This shouldn't change the API. If it did, we wouldn't be able to do this.

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] > a Count int also needs either +optional or +required.

It looks like we already have the marker for this in the schema.

> This shouldn't change the API. If it did, we wouldn't be able to do this.

Could you elaborate on this? I'm curious if adding a marker like +optional or +required is considered an API change in this context, and what the specific constraints are that would prevent us from modifying the API if needed?

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] I can indeed not find a plain value in the resource.k8s.io API which doesn't already have one or the other marker.

https://github.com/troychiu/kubernetes/blob/59a00b9f6c401b416a5c0de4cd70f07c15e64dfe/staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go#L1892C1-L1893C80

is a slice without them.

> I'm curious if adding a marker like +optional or +required is considered an API change in this context

If the marker matches what was valid before, then it isn't. But that's what needs to be checked. If any of the specs had been valid when empty, then `+optional` would be the right marker, not `+required`. When adding `+required` by mistake instead of `+optional`, it becomes an API change (previously valid data no longer is).

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] Thank you for your explanation! I tried with an empty spec and it did went through. In this case, I think `+optional` would be the right marker.

```
➜ cat empty-spec-resource-claim.yaml
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  name: empty-spec
➜ k apply -f empty-spec-resource-claim.yaml
resourceclaim.resource.k8s.io/empty-spec created
➜ k get resourceclaim empty-spec -o yaml
apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1
kind: ResourceClaim
metadata:
  annotations:
    kubectl.kubernetes.io/last-applied-configuration: |
      {"apiVersion":"resource.k8s.io/v1","kind":"ResourceClaim","metadata":{"annotations":{},"name":"empty-spec","namespace":"default"}}
  creationTimestamp: "2026-02-12T00:18:14Z"
  name: empty-spec
  namespace: default
  resourceVersion: "1467686"
  uid: 64e72d6c-04e1-41ba-8488-9608362e52af
spec:
  devices:
    requests: null
status: {}
```

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] Good catch. We do indeed allow the empty claim for "I don't need to allocate anything". References to it in pods then can be kept and the pods get scheduled just fine. 

For the same reason, ResourceClaimTemplate also allows the empty spec.

DeviceClass also allows empty spec. It's perhaps less useful, but there's also no required field in it.

The only required spec is in ResourceSlice:
```
The ResourceSlice "empty-spec" is invalid: 
* spec.driver: Required value
* spec.pool.name: Required value
* spec.pool.resourceSliceCount: Invalid value: 0: must be greater than zero
* spec: Required value: exactly one of `nodeName`, `nodeSelector`, `allNodes`, `perDeviceNodeSelection` is required
```

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] Oh thank you. I think what I can do is
1. Test each kind of spec with an empty one and see the behavior
2. Mark the fields with corresponding marker to make sure there is no API change.

I'll post the result for reference.

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] Docs for the linters are over [here](https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kube-api-linter/blob/main/docs/linters.md#optionalorrequired)

For these PRs, our hope is to enable this rule by API group as there are some groups with many many exceptions.

For each field we are changing, we must assess both the validation and defaulting code to understand the desired behaviour, and make sure that the relevant tags are added. We are not considering this an API change per se, because it doesn't change the actual behaviour. It does mean we have more complete openapi schemas, which can help folks out, and sets the way for later when we start doing more with declarative validation and generating validations rather than hand rolling them

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] > In this case, the struct contains required fields, so this wouldn't have been valid:
>
>{
>   ...
>
>    "spec": {}
>}
> If it was, then leaving out the "spec" entry would have been okay before and now would raise an error.

So in this case, we added also `nonpointstruct` after conversation at Kubecon where we decided that the right thing to do here for these non-pointer structs is to mark them up to match the implicit behaviour of the validation.

So if the struct has required fields or otherwise requires at least one value to be set (unions), it must be required

If it contains only optional fields, it is optional.

The go code isn't actually validating this, but it helps to complete the picture

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] > So if the struct has required fields or otherwise requires at least one value to be set (unions), it must be required
>

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] it looks like ValidateDeviceClass → validateDeviceClassSpec doesn't require and fields in spec be set, so +optional seems correct

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] it looks like nothing in ValidateResourceClaimTemplate → validateResourceClaimSpec → validateDeviceClaim requires fields under spec to be populated, so +optional seems correct

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] it looks like nothing in ValidateResourceClaimTemplate → validateResourceClaimSpec → validateDeviceClaim requires fields under spec to be populated, so +optional seems correct

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go] Thank you @liggitt for the review. They are already required.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb8032bb8313640f57d32560b90269618524e9c6/staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1/types.go#L104

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb8032bb8313640f57d32560b90269618524e9c6/staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1beta1/types.go#L89

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/eb8032bb8313640f57d32560b90269618524e9c6/staging/src/k8s.io/api/resource/v1beta2/types.go#L89

Adding `+required` is okay, I don't think we had a single spec that could have been left out without making the result invalid.

I'm just wondering why this comes up.

If we were to wait until https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134675 is merged, this enables the `nonpointerstructs` rule, which covers all of the cases here and would help us to make sure the right required/optional tag is being added

As discussed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/136935#discussion_r2797251344, the only required spec is ResourceSliceSpec. Interestingly, it was already marked as such in v1beta1 and v1beta2. We lost that in v1.

v1alpha3 has only DeviceTaintRule where spec is already `+required`.

/lgtm

title: fix: show only effective default StorageClass in kubectl output
human_review:
[pkg/registry/storage/storageclass/storage/storage.go] This is not the correct place where you want to change this. This ensures we have a generic mechanism working across all of the resources. You want to change the actual function responsible for printing the StorageClass resource, which is located here: 
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/97bd924010a39b71d3fd802e4284418c8b79545c/pkg/printers/internalversion/printers.go#L2648-L2677

[pkg/registry/storage/storageclass/storage/storage.go] Thanks for the review @soltysh.

Yes, I initially tried to implement this in `printStorageClass` as you suggested. However, the function only receives a single StorageClass object, so it cannot determine which one is the effective default among multiple StorageClasses with the default annotation.

When multiple StorageClasses have the default annotation, `kubectl get storageclass` could potentially be fixed in `printStorageClassList` since it has access to the full list. 
But for `kubectl get storageclass <name>`, only a single StorageClass object is passed to `printStorageClass`, so any StorageClass with the default annotation would still be shown as "(default)" even if it's not the effective default.

To identify the effective default in both cases, we need to compare creation timestamps across all StorageClasses. That's why I implemented a custom `TableConvertor` that can list all StorageClasses before generating the table.

Is there an alternative approach you would suggest?

[pkg/registry/storage/storageclass/storage/storage.go] @jaehanbyun I'd say that I prefer best effort than 100% correctness in that case. Let's go with updating `printStorageClassList` based on your suggestion, and when a single storage class is requested we'll abstain from providing information if that's the default or not. This will ensure we have consistency in the code, and we provide best effort value, based on the provided data.

[pkg/registry/storage/storageclass/storage/storage.go] @soltysh Thanks for the follow-up feedback. Updated as you suggested. PTAL.


```

$ kubectl get storageclass standard
NAME       PROVISIONER               RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE   ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE
standard   kubernetes.io/host-path   Delete          Immediate           false                  55s

$ kubectl get storageclass nfs-client

nfs-client   k8s-sigs.io/nfs-subdir-external-provisioner   Delete          Immediate           false                  1s
```

(both `standard` and `nfs-client` have the default annotation, `nfs-client` was created more recently)

/lgtm

[pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go] We shouldn't bind the scheduler internals with specific plugins, but rather make the framework generic and let the plugins use that logic to express their intent.

In case of this issue, one option can be to allow gang scheduling plugin to register specifically on unscheduled pod add event. Other plugins can register only for assigned pod add events when they need to. In fact, we would like to introduce something similar to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127387.

[pkg/scheduler/backend/queue/scheduling_queue.go] Done,
I have removed the specific function for GangScheduling, and now GangScheduling plugin registers UnscheduledAddPod event instead of AddPod, and modified tests accordingly making sure that MoveAllToActiveOrBackoffQueue is not invoking other plugins along for such event.

[pkg/scheduler/framework/plugins/gangscheduling/gangscheduling.go] This still mean the other plugins' queueing hints will be executed when the event is for unscheduled pod. +WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
+See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
+limitations under the License.
+*/
+
+package tableconvertor
+
+import (
+	"context"
+	"sort"
+	"strings"
+	"time"
+
+	apiextensions "k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions"
+	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/api/meta"
+	metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
+	"k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/runtime"
+	"k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/registry/rest"
+)
+
+var metaDocs = metav1.ObjectMeta{}.SwaggerDoc()
+
+func New() rest.TableConvertor { return &crdConvertor{} }
+
+type crdConvertor struct{}
+
+// ConvertToTable satisfies rest.TableConvertor.
+func (c *crdConvertor) ConvertToTable(ctx context.Context, obj runtime.Object, tableOpts runtime.Object) (*metav1.Table, error) {
+	table := &metav1.Table{}
+
+	if opt, _ := tableOpts.(*metav1.TableOptions); opt == nil || !opt.NoHeaders {
+		table.ColumnDefinitions = []metav1.TableColumnDefinition{
+			{Name: "Name", Type: "string", Format: "name", Description: metaDocs["name"]},
+			{Name: "Scope", Type: "string", Description: "Cluster/Namespaced"},
+			{Name: "Versions", Type: "string", Description: "Served versions"},
+			{Name: "Created At", Type: "date", Description: metaDocs["creationTimestamp"]},
+			{Name: "Group", Type: "string", Priority: 1, Description: "API group"},
+			{Name: "Kind", Type: "string", Priority: 1, Description: "CustomResource kind"},
+			{Name: "ShortNames", Type: "string", Priority: 1, Description: "Short names"},
+			{Name: "Established", Type: "boolean", Priority: 1, Description: "Established status"},
+		}
+	}
+
+	addRow := func(cr *apiextensions.CustomResourceDefinition) {
+		// versions: only served=true
+		var versions []string
+		for _, v := range cr.Spec.Versions {
+			if v.Served {
+				label := v.Name
+				if v.Storage {
+					label += "(storage)"
+				}
+				versions = append(versions, label)
+			}
+		}
+		sort.Strings(versions)
+
+		shortNames := strings.Join(cr.Spec.Names.ShortNames, ",")
+
+		table.Rows = append(table.Rows, metav1.TableRow{
+			Object: runtime.RawExtension{Object: cr},
+			Cells: []interface{}{
+				cr.Name,
+				string(cr.Spec.Scope),
+				strings.Join(versions, ","),
+				cr.CreationTimestamp.Time.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339),
+				cr.Spec.Group,
+				cr.Spec.Names.Kind,
+				shortNames,
+				isEstablished(cr),
+			},
+		})
+	}
+
+	switch {
+	case meta.IsListType(obj):
+		_ = meta.EachListItem(obj, func(item runtime.Object) error {
+			if cr, ok := item.(*apiextensions.CustomResourceDefinition); ok {
+				addRow(cr)
+			}
+			return nil
+		})
+	default:
+		if cr, ok := obj.(*apiextensions.CustomResourceDefinition); ok {
+			addRow(cr)
+		}
+	}
+
+	if l, err := meta.ListAccessor(obj); err == nil {
+		table.ResourceVersion = l.GetResourceVersion()
+		table.Continue = l.GetContinue()
+		table.RemainingItemCount = l.GetRemainingItemCount()
+	} else if m, err := meta.CommonAccessor(obj); err == nil {
+		table.ResourceVersion = m.GetResourceVersion()
+	}
+
+	return table, nil
+}
+
+// isEstablished returns true if the CRD has the Established condition with Status=True.
+func isEstablished(crd *apiextensions.CustomResourceDefinition) bool {
+	for _, cond := range crd.Status.Conditions {
+		if cond.Type == apiextensions.Established && cond.Status == apiextensions.ConditionTrue {
+			return true
+		}
+	}
+	return false
+}

title: e2e: dra: add delayed ResourceClaimTemplate test
human_review:
[test/e2e/dra/dra.go] Instead of checking the result of a Go expression, it's better to do the same check with a gomega matcher. In this case, check the list of claims for one which has the right name prefix.

Then if for some reason we get a claim generated that doesn't match the expected pattern, gomega will dump the existing claims. As it stands now we don't get any information about them in case of a failure.

[test/e2e/dra/dra.go] The more interesting case for the current problem is to create a pod with two template references, create the first template, wait for the first claim, then create the second template.
[test/e2e/dra/dra.go] => https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138504

AFAICT, the only place that this is used is here: 
  
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d3b1672d10572419f927c365ed1e75480a87280d/pkg/kubelet/pleg/evented.go#L196-L198

so why not move the wrapped Stop and Start calls inline?

```

	g.Start()

This logs instead of failing, which is inconsistent with other cleanup steps. Consider using `framework.Failf` or at least `framework.ExpectNoError` to catch cleanup issues.

[pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go] Thanks for catching that! "Academic state" was a typo in the comment. I meant to refer to the pod's last known state as recorded in the API server. I'll correct the comment to be clearer, something like: "the pod's last known state from the API server" to avoid ambiguity.

[pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go] Yes, the SyncTerminatedPod flow is the precise context where this fix is needed.

When a pod is rejected at admission, the status manager immediately sets its phase to Failed.
After a Kubelet restart, the pod worker for this now-terminal pod is initialized. Since the pod is already terminal, the worker bypasses the SyncPod and SyncTerminatingPod stages and goes directly to the cleanup phase, which invokes SyncTerminatedPod.
SyncTerminatedPod then calls generateAPIPodStatus to create the final status update. This is the exact point where the bug occurred, the function would incorrectly generate ContainerStatusUnknown.

[pkg/kubelet/kubelet_pods.go] The goal is to uniquely identify a pod that was rejected by the Kubelet's own admission controller and never had any containers created for it. This situation becomes problematic only after a Kubelet restart, when our in-memory runtime cache is empty.
The most reliable source of truth in this scenario is the combination of three signals:
 
 - The Pod's Last Known Status from the API Server (pod.Status): This is our "ground truth" from before the restart. The key signal here is that the pod is in a terminal phase (Failed or Succeeded) without any containerStatuses. A pod that successfully ran and then terminated would have container statuses recorded. Their absence is a strong indicator that no containers were ever created.
 - The Kubelet's Current Runtime State (podStatus): After a restart, the Kubelet's view of the container runtime is empty for this pod (isEmptyRuntimeStatus is true). This confirms that there are no running or recently exited containers that we need to account for.
 - The Current State of the Pod Worker (podIsTerminal): This confirms that the pod worker is in the cleanup phase (SyncTerminatedPod), which is the correct context for this logic to run.

The check for v1.PodSucceeded is included for completeness, although it's a less common scenario for admission rejection. A pod with a RestartPolicy of Never could theoretically be rejected by a webhook, complete its (zero) containers, and move to Succeeded. While rare, including it makes the check more comprehensive.
Essentially, the combination of "is terminal in API server" + "has no container statuses in API server" + "has no running containers in runtime" forms a unique signature for a pod that was rejected at admission and never ran. This combination is highly unlikely to occur under any other circumstance.

title: Mirror List and WatchList tracing
human_review: [staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] I think that `SetListOptionsDefaults` should be moved up, right after the parameter decoding and before isWatch/isWatchList.
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] Maybe we should move `ValidateListOptions` too.

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] I think that the span is never ended (no defer call) on error paths (e.g. line 196).
Is this OK?
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] should the span be also ended for Watch request ?
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] should we update this comment? (now it also tracks WatchList req)

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] This doesn't change. We didn't end the span before as it requires passing `logThreshold` for the tracing util library, the minimal duration after span is treated as slow and will be logged. We don't want to have trace logs for 10 minute watches that were requested by client to be 10 minutes. We want to trace the initial events collection part of watch. The List in WatchList
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] Any reason? To identify WatchList we need to at least parse options, other things can be done as part of the span.

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] > Any reason? 

`SetListOptionsDefaults` modifies the `ListOptions`. So to properly detect a "WatchList" request for all cases (legacy) I think we should move it up. Does it make sense?

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] In case OpenTelemetry is enabled, it will create otel Span which *must* be `Ended` per documentation: https://pkg.go.dev/go.opentelemetry.io/otel/trace#Tracer
> Any Span that is created MUST also be ended. This is the responsibility of the user.
> Implementations of this API may leak memory or other resources if Spans are not ended.

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] We are not changing span ending here! Span was never ended before for Watch. We are changing behavior for WatchList, Watch span maintains untouched.

See line 300:
```
-		// Log only long List requests (ignore Watch).
-		defer span.End(500 * time.Millisecond)
```

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] The previous implementation was wrong and leaked memory when any error occured before L300. Let's change it as we are changing tracing in this file (or fix the memleak in different PR merged before this one)

[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] > leaked memory when any error occured before L300

Watch never reached L300, errors didn't matter. We should separate bug fixes and features. Recommend to move concerns about memory leak to separate issue.
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/handlers/get.go] Yikes!  We definitely should be ending all spans, but we can move that to a separate issue.

[test/integration/apiserver/tracing/tracing_test.go] Ah, looks like this was probably an oversight on my part in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/127053. I thought this span had disappeared and removed it to fix tests.  Looks like it didn't actually?

  789 status_manager.go:920] updateLastTransitionTime: pod=default/slow-image-pull-pod [PodReadyToStartContainers] ENTRY - currentStatus=False, currentLastTransitionTime=0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC (IsZero=true)
  789 status_manager.go:934] updateLastTransitionTime: pod=default/slow-image-pull-pod [PodReadyToStartContainers] no oldCondition found, setting new time: 2026-02-07 13:49:30.409056436 +0000 UTC m=+33.082749891
  789 status_manager.go:937] updateLastTransitionTime: pod=default/slow-image-pull-pod [PodReadyToStartContainers] PRE EXIT - condition.LastTransitionTime=0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC (IsZero=true)
  789 status_manager.go:940] updateLastTransitionTime: pod=default/slow-image-pull-pod [PodReadyToStartContainers] EXIT - condition.LastTransitionTime=2026-02-07 13:49:30.409056436 +0000 UTC m=+33.082749891 (IsZero=false)
  ```

- BUt now, at this point, when it enters `OnPodSandboxReady` function,

  it find the cached `PodReadyToStartContainers` condition (`status="False" LastTransitionTime="2026-02-07 13:49:30.409056436 +0000 UTC"`) -> 
  and update it to (`status="True" LastTransitionTime="001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC"`) again.

  ```
  789 kubelet.go:3418] "OnPodSandboxReady: existing PodReadyToStartContainers condition found" pod="default/slow-image-pull-pod" Status="False" LastTransitionTime="2026-02-07 13:49:30 +0000 UTC" IsZero=false
  
  789 kubelet.go:3433] "OnPodSandboxReady: created readySandboxCondition" pod="default/slow-image-pull-pod" Status="True" LastTransitionTime="0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC" IsZero=true
  
  789 kubelet.go:3451] "OnPodSandboxReady: after ReplaceOrAppendPodCondition" pod="default/slow-image-pull-pod" Status="True" LastTransitionTime="0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC" IsZero=true
  ```

   And so at this point, the PodReadyToStartContainers is updated again in the cache 
   `{Status="True" LastTransitionTime="0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC"}`


- Now when from within `OnPodSandboxReady`,  `SetPodStatus` function is called:
  
  ```
  kl.statusManager.SetPodStatus(logger, pod, existingStatus)
  ```

  which it in turn calls `updateLastTransitionTime` for the second time.

   This time, no change happens in the `LastTransitionTime` because it finds no change between current and the cached PodReadyToSTartContainers condition status - 

  ```
  789 status_manager.go:920] updateLastTransitionTime: pod=default/slow-image-pull-pod [PodReadyToStartContainers] ENTRY - currentStatus=True, currentLastTransitionTime=0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC (IsZero=true)
  
  789 status_manager.go:928] updateLastTransitionTime: pod=default/slow-image-pull-pod [PodReadyToStartContainers] INSIDE IF LOOP - oldStatus=True, oldLastTransitionTime=0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC, condition.LastTransitionTime=0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC (IsZero=true)
  
  789 status_manager.go:937] updateLastTransitionTime: pod=default/slow-image-pull-pod [PodReadyToStartContainers] PRE EXIT - condition.LastTransitionTime=0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC (IsZero=true)
  
  789 status_manager.go:940] updateLastTransitionTime: pod=default/slow-image-pull-pod [PodReadyToStartContainers] EXIT - condition.LastTransitionTime=0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC (IsZero=true)
  ```

  And so,  PodReadyToStartContainers still remains - `{Status="True" LastTransitionTime="0001-01-01 00:00:00 +0000 UTC"}`

and this is what fails [these e2e tests - `pod_conditions_test.go#L230-L240`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/d863fbe80b374c886453d23f7dfef60cac0f06e5/test/e2e_node/pod_conditions_test.go#L230-L240) because, at this point in the flow, the tests expects a  non-zero `LastTransitionTime` for PodReadyToStartContainers which is not the case if we don't set `LastTransitionTime` in `OnPodSandboxReady`. 

And setting the `LastTransitionTime` fixes this.

[pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go] This is exactly what I'm saying. Directly modifying the condition in the `existingStatus` obtained from `statusManager.GetPodStatus` will indeed update the `PodStatus` in the cache. So what you need is a `DeepCopy`, not redundant code to mask the issue.

[pkg/kubelet/kubelet.go] Ah correct. Sorry, I truly didn't catch the "need to create a deep copy before updating pod status" part until you mentioned above.

I have updated it in the PR now. Thank you so much once again :pray:

title: Add request_content_type_total counter to track Protobuf migration
human_review:
[staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/endpoints/metrics/metrics.go] ```suggestion
		[]string{"verb", "group", "resource", "media_type"},
```
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/131796

Thanks for the PR.

**Cardinality concern**
I'm a bit worried about the cardinality impact here. apiserver_request_duration_seconds is a stable histogram with 23 buckets, so each unique label combination creates 26 Prometheus series. The existing labels already produce thousands of series on a busy cluster — adding content_type (up to 4 values) would multiply that by 3-4x.

Could you share a rough estimate of the series increase on a representative cluster?

If the main goal is spotting clients that haven't migrated to protobuf, would a dedicated counter work instead? Something like:
```
apiserver_request_content_type_total{verb, content_type, resource} counter
```
That'd give you the same visibility at a fraction of the cost (1 series per combination vs 26).

[staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go] Good catch! This behavior was dropped as a part of this change and there was no test covering it.

This is difficult to reproduce without adding a redundant API call in the `infos` loop, similarly to what has been done before inside describers.
```
for _, info := range infos {
  resource, err := client.Get(info.Name, info.Namespace, ...) // the API call
}
```
This is because `resource.Builder` returns a list of aggregated errors consisting of `APIStatus` errors:
```
{
  "kind": "Status",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "metadata": {},
  "status": "Failure",
  "message": "pods \"testaaaaaaaa\" not found",
  "reason": "NotFound",
  "details": {
    "name": "testaaaaaaaa",
    "kind": "pods"
  },
  "code": 404
}
```
And there is no way to correlate them with`Info` they have been thrown for to be able to reliably retrieve `{namespace, name, kind}` from them (needed for events retrieval).
This information is essentially missed here:
```
func (i *Info) Get() (err error) {
	obj, err := NewHelper(i.Client, i.Mapping).WithSubresource(i.Subresource).Get(i.Namespace, i.Name)
	if err != nil {
		// code skipped for clarity
		return err
	}
	i.Object = obj
	i.ResourceVersion, _ = metadataAccessor.ResourceVersion(obj)
	return nil
}
```

I also investigated the possibility to call `Visit` on the `resource.Builder` instead of calling `Infos()`.
```
.Do().Visit(func (info *resource.Info, err error) error {
    // handle info or error for info	
})
```
But visitor function is not being called for errored infos.

Among the solutions I see for this is:
- Add this network call to explicitly and always re-fetch the resource in `infos` loop and drop `Latest().` call. This in cases when user is doing `kubectl get pod foo` will make request for the resource twice (this is already happening in the production code).
- Patch `Info.Get()` to return error type encapsulating both the original error and `Info` it is for.
- Drop this behavior (preferred as it makes things optimal and code simpler)

What do you think is the best way to move forward on this?

[staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go] This is now just doing a type check on the object instance passed in, not checking if the server supports v2.

That means if you have a manifest containing a v1 HPA, and you do `kubectl describe -f hpa.yaml`, kubectl will fetch the matching version from the server (with `Latest()`) and then pass that to this function to describe.

That means describe of objects in a manifest now uses the API version in the manifest to describe. Maybe that's ok, but that needs to be explicitly decided, not just accidentally switched here.

Let's start a list of the known behavior changes involved in this PR in the description
* Describing a v1 HPA object from a manifest (`kubectl describe -f v1hpa.yaml`) now describes the v1 version, rather than preferring v2 from the API
* Describing a pod from a manifest (`kubectl describe -f pod.yaml`) which no longer exists no longer displays events related to that pod
* ... anything else?
[staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go] I dropped this behavior in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135281 and it is no longer a part of this PR.

[staging/src/k8s.io/kubectl/pkg/describe/describe.go] 1. Can we just accept this behavior change and maybe note it in release notes only?
2. This behavior was dropped in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135281 and is no longer a concern

A few suggestions to drop deprecated and removed APIs. kubectl supports [+/-1 versions](https://kubernetes.io/releases/version-skew-policy/#kubectl), so no need to keep removed, or not supported/not served versions anymore.

> Secondary data like events is still retrieved. Events itself can be skipped using `--show-events=false` flag.

I still think we need to address the existing default behavior, not count on the user to opt out of pathological fetching. I'm not sure if it would make sense to do in a separate PR or in a commit in this PR.

[pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/topology_hints.go] You're right that the current tests only cover device hint generation in isolation. However, this PR doesn't modify the TopologyManager merge path at all, it only changes which NUMA nodes the device manager iterates over when building its hint list. The merge logic in `policy.Merge() / HintMerger` is untouched and already covered by `commonPolicyMergeTestCases` in `policy_test.go` (which uses multiple mock providers with various hint combinations under best-effort and restricted).
The key to verify is that the output of `generateDeviceTopologyHints` remains compatible with merge, specifically that a broad enough hint exists for intersection. `TestGenerateDeviceTopologyHintsAddsDefaultMaskWhenFiltered` validates exactly that: the non-preferred full-machine mask is appended when candidate NUMA nodes are narrowed.
A full integration test wiring real device+CPU+memory managers through Admit() doesn't exist today in the codebase and would be a significant new test pattern. I think that would be valuable as a follow-up but is out of scope for this bug fix. Happy to file an issue to track it.

This is a very good point! There is no existing validation on device topology NUMA IDs at registration time, so a buggy device plugin could report arbitrary NUMA node IDs.
I've added an explicit runtime subset guard in `deviceNUMANodes()`: the returned set is now intersected with `m.numaNodes` (the cadvisor-reported NUMA topology), and any unknown NUMA IDs are logged and dropped:
```go
knownNodes := sets.New[int](m.numaNodes...)
unknown := nodesWithDevices.Difference(knownNodes)
if unknown.Len() > 0 {
    klog.InfoS("Ignoring NUMA node IDs reported by device plugin that are unknown to cadvisor",
        "resource", resource, "unknownNodes", sets.List(unknown), "knownNodes", m.numaNodes)
    nodesWithDevices = nodesWithDevices.Intersection(knownNodes)
}
```
The returned set is now guaranteed to be a subset of m.numaNodes, regardless of what device plugins report. I also added a new test case ("unknown NUMA IDs from device plugin are dropped") validates this behavior.

Thanks for the fix @fanzhangio — the livelock on GB200 is a real problem and this PR clearly addresses it. I have one suggestion that I think would strengthen the case for landing this as a bug fix and make it more backport-friendly.

### Concern: behavioral change in `Preferred` flags

`candidateNUMANodes()` filters on `available ∪ reusable` devices, which excludes NUMA nodes where all devices are allocated to other pods. This changes `minAffinitySize` computation and consequently which hints get marked `Preferred`.

Example: NUMA [0, 1, 2], request=2. Node 1 has 5 devices all allocated (0 available), nodes 0 and 2 each have 1 available device.

- **Current code:** `minAffinitySize=1` (node 1's 5 total devices satisfy the threshold). Hint {0,2} gets `Preferred=false`.
- **This PR:** `candidateNUMANodes=[0,2]`, `minAffinitySize=2`. Hint {0,2} gets `Preferred=true`.

This is arguably better behavior, but it is a behavioral change, not just a performance fix. That makes it harder to justify as a backportable bug fix.

### Suggestion: filter on all devices for the resource, not just available+reusable

If we collect NUMA nodes from `m.allDevices[resource]` (all devices regardless of allocation state) instead of `available.Union(reusable)`, the fix becomes behavior-preserving:

```go
deviceNUMANodes := sets.New[int]()
for _, device := range m.allDevices[resource] {
    deviceNUMANodes.Insert(m.getNUMANodeIds(device.Topology)...)
}
if deviceNUMANodes.Len() == 0 {
    deviceNUMANodes = sets.New[int](m.numaNodes...)
}

bitmask.IterateBitMasks(sets.List(deviceNUMANodes), func(mask bitmask.BitMask) {
```

This still solves the O(2^n) livelock — on GB200, devices reside on 1-2 NUMA nodes, so iteration drops from 2^36 to 2^2 regardless of which filtering approach is used. But because all device-bearing nodes remain in the iteration (including those with fully-allocated devices), `minAffinitySize` and `Preferred` flags are preserved.

The rationale is also simpler to defend as a bug fix: "NUMA nodes with zero devices for a resource should not be enumerated in that resource's hint generation." Including them produces no useful hints — masks covering only device-less nodes always fail the `numMatching < request` check and are discarded. On large-NUMA systems this wasted enumeration becomes unbounded.

This also removes the need for the synthetic fallback hint (the `len(candidateNUMANodes) < len(m.numaNodes)` block), since `minAffinitySize` is unchanged and the intermediate non-preferred hints lost are strictly wider than existing hints and never selected by TopologyManager.

### Path forward

The available+reusable filtering, the `Preferred` improvement, and the `candidateNUMANodes` helper as currently proposed are all good changes — they could land as a follow-up PR. But if the goal is to land a bug fix that's backportable to 1.36, keeping the scope to the behavior-preserving version gives it the cleanest path through review.

title: Use +k8s:minItems on a required list field
human_review:
[staging/src/k8s.io/api/scheduling/v1alpha2/types.go] This feels redundant.

+k8s:required and +k8s:minItems=1 are the same things here for DV.


I think you are thinking about the convergence between OpenAPI required and +k8s:required here. In this case, the criteria for both are already met. It is both OpenAPI required and DV required.


Earlier we considered adding `+k8s:zeroValueAllowed(https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136897)` to provide a path to converge with openAPI required and DV required. We later found that we can change the OpenAPI `required` field to optional(or vice versa) if we encounter scenarios where both +k8s:required and +required can't be used together.
[staging/src/k8s.io/api/scheduling/v1alpha2/types.go] If we ever find that we need `+required` and `+k8s:optional` on the same field (or vice-versa) I think we will have lost the plot.

[staging/src/k8s.io/api/scheduling/v1alpha2/types.go] I did an analysis  in the past as part of https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136897.  There are a few cases where it is possible. We have consensus to change +required to optional in those cases. This will be backward compatible, because we never had a check for openapi required.  It was also done as part of KAL effort, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/135470, Here priorityClass.Value was converted from openAPI required(in the schema) to optional.


blurb from https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/136897#issuecomment-3881230972
```
I was discussing with @liggitt . He suggests that if a field can take a zero value and still work, it should be optional with respect to the open API and DV. 
```

+// InformerSyncHealthChecker is a health checker that verifies all informers have synced their caches.
+type InformerSyncHealthChecker struct {
+	controllerName string
+	syncFuncs      []cache.InformerSynced
+}
+
+// NewInformerSyncHealthChecker creates a new InformerSyncHealthChecker that verifies
+// all informers have synced their caches.
+func NewInformerSyncHealthChecker(controllerName string, syncFuncs ...cache.InformerSynced) healthz.HealthChecker {

+		syncFuncs:      syncFuncs,

+// It returns immediately without blocking; it does not wait for caches to sync.
+func (c *InformerSyncHealthChecker) Check(_ *http.Request) error {

+	return fmt.Sprintf("informer-sync-%s", c.controllerName)

human_review: [build/dependencies.yaml] Dont we need to mention `dependents` here?

[build/dependencies.yaml] that might break someone.

it's not consistent across the file. the original idea was to have:
1. `- name: some-dep` as the place that is the source of truth e.g. a Makefile
2. `- name: some-dep: dependents` as the places where the version is used

but this also opens up for cases where someone updates 1 and missed 2, thus a drift again.

dependencies.yaml is technically machine consumable so my change is also breaking, but arguably nobody read  `- name: "registry.k8s.io/pause: dependents"`, that matters locally for the repo and the `: dependents` suffixes were overall redundant.

if that's a concern i can keep them in separate items.

[build/dependencies.yaml] @neolit123 I think it's required to keep them in separate items. To my knowledge, the way this is supposed to work is:

- You update `build/pause/Makefile` to trigger a new image build
- You promote the resulting image by creating and merging a PR in k/k8s.io
- You update dependents

Because this is a multi-step task that depends on an external step (promotion), you can't trigger the build and update usages in a single PR.

That said, if you were to build 3.10.3 after this change, you wouldn't be able to merge a k/k PR that would trigger that build, as you would update only Makefile, but dependency checks would be failing because dependents are still on a previous versions. And you can't update dependents because the new version doesn't exist and is not promoted yet.

I hope this makes sense, I know it's messy, but tl;dr is that it's important to keep them in separate items.

[build/dependencies.yaml] Nit: now that I'm thinking about this, if pause version will always contain PATCH, maybe this and other entries should be updated to `\d+\.\d+\.\d+` to properly match `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`
[build/dependencies.yaml] good point, updated to match the 3rd digit too.
IMO, this looks like something that should be merged for .0, but the comment should/must be addressed before merging it.

/lgtm
/approve
cc @kubernetes/release-team-leads for decision on should this be included in the .0 release
Just one nit, shouldn't be blocking as long as the job is passing.

+	lock     sync.RWMutex
+	clients  map[chan PodWatchEvent]struct{}
+	incoming chan PodWatchEvent

+func NewBroadcaster() *broadcaster {
+	b := &broadcaster{
+		clients:  make(map[chan PodWatchEvent]struct{}),

+func (b *broadcaster) run() {

[staging/src/k8s.io/kubelet/pkg/apis/pods/v1alpha1/api.proto] We cannot reference Kubernetes REST API types from protoc-generated GRPC APIs.

The Kubernetes API types are *not* generated as standard protoc messages ... mixing them into uses by grpc / protoc generated APIs is not something we should do. They were previously treated as "aberrant messages" in a best-effort way by the standard proto libraries, and with https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/134256 are no longer usable as proto messages by `google.golang.org/protobuf/proto`

xref https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/tree/master/keps/sig-api-machinery/5589-gogo-dependency#motivation for details

[pkg/controller/scheduling/podgroupprotection/podgroup_protection_controller.go] There is a race condition between the controller and the API server. Let me explain it in detail.

T0: The PodGroup protection controller and the API server are running, and the informers are synced.

T1: A PodGroup pg1 and a Pod pg1-pod1 are created. The PodGroup pg1 is deleted immediately after its creation.

T2: The scheduler schedules the pod before the delete event is received.

T3: The pod is running on a node.

T4: The controller receives the delete event for pg1 before the create event. As a result, the protection controller removes the finalizer from pg1 because we do not perform live lookups of Pods against the API server.

T5: Eventually, pg1 is deleted, and pg1-pod1 references a non-existent PodGroup.

Is this behavior expected? If we can avoid live lookups for Pods in the new protection controller, that would be ideal.

In the past, the PVC protection controller had a performance issue because it performed live lookups for Pods. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125372 improves the issue.

[pkg/apis/batch/validation/validation.go] Side note: Can we simplify the mental model for this PR and stop referring to "higher-level controllers" altogether?

I think the current confusion comes from mixing two separate pieces of logic:

1. Workload/PodGroup Creation & Attachment: This should happen IFF the Job is eligible AND PodTemplate.Spec.SchedulingGroup is not set. It genuinely doesn't matter who set it (user, JobSet, etc.).
2. Blocking parallelism mutation: This should happen IFF the Job uses gang scheduling.

What we missed in the KEP is that validating if a Job "uses gang scheduling" is inherently hard, because as @wojtek-t pointed out, it requires cross-checking the actual PodGroup object when users bring their own.

I'd err on the side of simplicity for Alpha. I suggest changing the validation criteria from "Does the Job use gang scheduling?" to "Did the Job controller create the Workload/PodGroup for gang scheduling?" (which perfectly aligns with logic 1).

This means if users bring their own PodGroup, we allow parallelism mutations. It's not ideal, but bring-your-own workload is already supported (even without this integration) and already has this problem. We can try fixing that via admission, but for me it's P2. Plus, long-term (targeting 1.37), we plan to allow MinCount mutations anyway, which makes this problem disappear.

TL;DR: The code itself seems correct, but the comments and our mental model need adjusting.

[staging/src/k8s.io/code-generator/cmd/validation-gen/output_tests/tags/featuregate/zz_generated.validations.go] Historically, handwritten validation did not implement "if it is unchanged, leave it alone" like DV does, so the rule was to validate a field if the option was set (almost always defined as gate-enabled or in-use).

This means that a field could change values within the set of allowed values EVEN IF THE GATE WAS OFF, as long as it started with an allowed value.  If the option is not enabled, we just ignore it.  Mostly that is OK because of the in-use checks -- an opt should not be enabled when there is a value present.

Put another way, there are five possible paths:

1) gate-enabled
2) gate-disabled and not in use
3) gate-disabled, in use, unchanged
4) gate-disabled, in use, changed, valid
5) gate-disabled, in use, changed, invalid

Cases 1 and 2 are obvious.

DV ratcheting handles the #3 case (in-use and unchanged) automatically by allowing it to remain

The question is how we should handle cases 4 and 5.  Case 5 should obviously fail but the exact REASON depends on case 4.

title: Support TopologyManager in Large NUMA System (NVIDIA GB200)
human_review: [pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/topology_hints.go] please add testcase for adding defaultMask to returned hints when hints are limited to NUMA nodes where the devices are.
[pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/topology_hints.go] very good idea to only limit combinations to nodes where devices are.
[pkg/kubelet/cm/memorymanager/policy_static.go] does it mean that memory from NUMA nodes without CPU is unusable?

[pkg/kubelet/cm/memorymanager/policy_static.go] No, it doesn’t make the memory “unusable,” but it does stop the memory manager from proposing new placements on NUMA nodes that have no CPUs. It keeps hint search bounded to CPU-bearing nodes. If a CPU-less node already has allocations, it stays in the set and can be reused, existing assignments aren’t dropped. On the other side, the memory tables for those nodes remain in state, they’re just not chosen for new hints because there’s no CPU locality to attach them to.

[pkg/kubelet/cm/memorymanager/policy_static.go] I still don't get why do we check `NumberOfAssignments`? As an alternative can we just filter out NUMA nodes in memory manager without any available memory? to minimize number of hints?

[pkg/kubelet/cm/memorymanager/policy_static.go] IIUC, the key insight which drives this PR and mitigates the reported issue is that since the topology manager allows to allocate all the required resources on a single NUMA node, then it makes no sense to consider NUMA nodes which don't have memory AND cpus.
It's wasted effort because by definition we can't align all resources on nodes which don't even have resources in the first place (e.g. cpu-less memory node). 

I agree it's fine adding a pragmatic solution, but I'm a bit wary to add cpu-awareness in the memory manager, because it kinda breaks the specialization.
For the sake of pragmaticity this can fly, but then it would make sense to do the symmetrical check in cpumanager and rule out cpu-only NUMA nodes.

Ultimately, the gap IMO is in the hint merge logic because current HW highlights the assumption we had that all NUMA nodes are symmetric and all feature both memory and CPUs, and they may or may not have devices; IOW, the resource managers design doesn't expect fully non-overlapping nodes.
[pkg/kubelet/cm/memorymanager/policy_static.go] Ok. Dropped the NumberOfAssignments guard so memory-manager hint generation now simply skips NUMA nodes without CPUs for all cases.

[pkg/kubelet/cm/cpumanager/policy_static.go] Is there ever a case where `numaNodesWithMemory != numaNodes`? If there is, then let's continue the discussion on how this commit could be simplified. If there's not, I'm not convinced we need any changes to the `cpumanager` at all. My understanding is that we would never have a NUMA node associated with a CPU if it didn't also have memory attached to it.
[pkg/kubelet/cm/memorymanager/policy_static.go] I think you can use a [set](https://pkg.go.dev/k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/sets) for the type of `numaNodesWithCPUs` to simplify this.

[pkg/kubelet/cm/memorymanager/policy_static.go] I don't think we should do this. If there is some weird esoteric hardware that would require this, then the `TopologyManager` should not be used. We can advise them to just disable it. We should add a follow.up to improve the docs around this.

[pkg/kubelet/cm/devicemanager/topology_hints.go] Similar to my comment earlier, I don't think we should do this. If there is a system that requires this, they should not be enabling the `TopologyManager` in the first place.
Please split the change into 2 commits, one for memorymanager and second for devicemanager.

@fanzhangio, thanks for being patient while I took the time to look through this PR in detail.

Unfortunately, I don't think we can make this change without a KEP. When first discussing this PR on slack, I thought this problem could be cast as a bug fix for systems that online a bunch of "unusable" NUMA nodes from the perspective of the `TopologyManager`, but after careful consideration (and review of this PR), I don't think that's true anymore

Instead, I think we need to add a mode of operation where all hint providers only consider NUMA nodes where CPUs are attached. For the CPU manager this is already true (by definition), and for the MemoryManager and DeviceManager this would need to be protected by some sort of flag, so as not to break any existing use-cases.

This should take the form of a `TopologyManager` option, that gets propagated to all hint providers so that they only consider NUMA nodes that match this criteria.

I am happy to review / champion this KEP for the 1.36 time frame. Please feel free to ping me once you have something ready.
